CORRECTED (was wrong in an earlier pass of this file): state_publisher.py DOES set EpuckState.stamp (self.get_clock().now().to_msg()) -- the actual root cause of trial01's epoch-scale 'age' figures was analyze_comm_performance.py mixing rosbag2's own wall-clock recording timestamp with message.stamp (sim time), two different clock domains. Fixed (protocol_v1.1_stamp_semantics): state_publisher.py now holds publication (WAITING_FOR_CLOCK) until the clock is valid so stamp is never a fake zero; analyze_comm_performance.py's bag-based age computation now excludes negative/implausibly-large ages and reports latency_domain_mismatch_detected rather than silently averaging garbage in; sequence_counter.py now computes its own LIVE latency (message.stamp vs its own get_clock().now() at receipt, same clock domain, no mismatch) -- validated by objective5_timestamp_latency_validation_pilot01 and used for objective5_comm_baseline_zero_impairment_formal_trial02_stamp's latency=VALID coverage. PDR, rate, and bandwidth were never affected by this bug.

peer_timeout_s audit finding (read-only, frozen cooperative_avoider unmodified): peer freshness is judged by CALLBACK RECEIPT TIME (self._now_s() at the moment _peer_callback fires), not by msg.stamp. A fixed/constant relay delay does NOT necessarily trigger peer_timeout -- it only shifts the whole message stream later by a constant offset; the steady-state gap between consecutive receipts stays close to the publish period regardless of a constant delay. Only jitter (variance) or real message loss can plausibly cause a receipt gap large enough to exceed peer_timeout_s. An earlier matrix-design draft's claim that a 0.6s configured delay would trigger peer-timeout degradation is RETRACTED. Changing freshness semantics to use msg.stamp instead would be a new protocol/safety-version decision, not made this session.

network_impairment_relay.py audit finding: relay scheduling uses ROS/sim time (get_clock().now() under use_sim_time=true), so delay/jitter semantics do not drift with Webots realtime factor. jitter CAN cause reordering (the release-time min-heap flushes strictly by release_time, not receive order). drop/jitter use random.Random(seed), fully reproducible given the same seed. Relay CSV now also records source_stamp_s and actual_release_time_s (appended columns, existing readers keyed by column name unaffected).
